title: Naomi Bulochnikov‑Paul Exits Disney Entertainment Television as EVP of Communications – Deadline Report
body:
Naomi Bulochnikov‑Paul, who has spent the past eight years shaping the public‑facing narrative of Disney’s television division, announced her departure from the role of executive vice president of communications for Disney Entertainment Television. In an internal memo circulated to her team, Bulochnikov‑Paul confirmed that she will be leaving the company later this month, marking the end of a tenure that saw the launch of several high‑profile streaming initiatives and a major re‑branding of Disney’s linear networks.

During her time at Disney, Bulochnikov‑Paul oversaw communications strategy for a portfolio that includes ABC, Disney Channel, Freeform, and the rapidly expanding Disney+ and Hulu platforms. She was instrumental in guiding the messaging around the company’s pivot to a direct‑to‑consumer model, navigating both the excitement of new content rollouts and the challenges of industry‑wide disruptions caused by the pandemic. Colleagues describe her as a “steady hand” who blended data‑driven insights with a storyteller’s sensibility, helping Disney maintain a cohesive brand voice across a fragmented media landscape.

Industry observers note that Bulochnikov‑Paul’s exit comes at a pivotal moment for Disney’s television business. The company is in the midst of a multi‑year restructuring that seeks to streamline operations, cut costs, and integrate its streaming and linear assets under a unified leadership structure. Her departure may signal a further consolidation of the communications function, potentially merging it with the broader corporate communications team that reports directly to the chief communications officer. Such a move could enhance message consistency but also raises questions about how the nuanced needs of each network will be addressed moving forward.

The timing also aligns with Disney’s ongoing effort to recalibrate its content slate after a period of aggressive expansion. While Disney+ has surpassed 150 million subscribers worldwide, the company has faced subscriber churn and heightened competition from rivals such as Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and emerging players like Apple TV+. Bulochnikov‑Paul’s role in articulating the strategic rationale behind new releases, international rollouts, and partnership deals was critical in maintaining investor confidence and audience engagement. Her exit may therefore prompt a reevaluation of how Disney communicates its evolving content strategy to both the public and its shareholders.

Insiders suggest that Bulochnikov‑Paul’s next move could involve a senior communications position at another major media conglomerate or a shift toward consultancy work focused on brand transformation. Her reputation for steering complex, multi‑platform narratives makes her a coveted talent in an industry where reputation management is increasingly intertwined with data analytics and real‑time audience feedback. For Disney, the challenge will be to replace her expertise without losing momentum in an environment where every press release, social media post, and crisis response can influence subscriber numbers and advertising revenue.

Looking ahead, Disney Entertainment Television will likely appoint an interim leader while conducting a thorough search for a permanent EVP of communications. The new appointee will inherit a communications apparatus that must balance the legacy of linear television with the relentless pace of streaming innovation. As Disney continues to refine its content strategy and navigate the shifting sands of the entertainment market, the effectiveness of its messaging will remain a crucial component of its competitive edge. Bulochnikov‑Paul’s departure underscores the broader industry trend of senior communications talent moving between giants, reflecting the ever‑increasing importance of narrative control in the digital age.
